exceptions.cause: St Stephen: the old site says the Creed is not said; it is said on every day of the Christmas octave (Code of Rubrics n. 475d). The calendar follows the rubric.
Old-site typo (eloquiumvtum for eloquium tuum) in the offertory of Friday and Saturday after Ash Wednesday; corrected against Divinum Officium.
Old-site typos (qual, offerimum) in the secret of the 18th Sunday after Pentecost; corrected against Divinum Officium.
Old site labels the single prophetic lesson of some Ember Fridays Epístola and of others Léctio; the calendar uses Léctio whenever the reading is not from an Epistle.
Rogation Mass: the old site prints the Paschal Alleluia of the votive Mass for any necessity; the Missal's Rogation Mass has Alleluia. Confitemini Domino (Divinum Officium), which is kept.
St Joseph the Worker: the old site has the Croatian postcommunion in the Latin column; Latin from Divinum Officium.
Ascension: the old site's rank line says Nedjelja (Sunday); it is a feast of I class.
Queenship of Our Lady: for the commemoration of St Petronilla the old site repeats the secret of the feast; the calendar gives St Petronilla's own secret.
St Augustine: the old site prints the verse Inveni David without Alleluia; Divinum Officium has Alleluia. Amavit eum. Kept from Divinum Officium (listed for review).
Maternity of Our Lady: the old site omits the word Alleluia around the verse; text otherwise the same.
Sts Simon and Jude: the old site prints the Alleluia verse and Gospel of St James (Mt 20); the Missal has Nimis honorati and Jn 15, 17-25 (Divinum Officium).
Chair of St Peter: the old site continues the offertory with 'et quodcumque ligaveris…'; the Missal's antiphon ends at 'claves regni caelorum' (Divinum Officium).
St Francis Caracciolo: old site 'sicut cedrus Libani', Missal 'sicut cedrus, quae in Libano est' (Divinum Officium).
Saturday Mass of Our Lady in Paschaltide: the old site prints the antiphon three times.
Holy Thursday evening Mass: the old site inserts the washing of the feet (antiphons) after the Gospel; the calendar shows the Mandatum with the rites of Holy Week.
